(فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ مَشْهَدِ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ): The فاء is a conjunction; وويل is a mubtadaʾ, and it is permissible to begin with an indefinite noun because it includes the meaning of supplication; وللذين is the khabar of ويل; the clause كفروا is the ṣila; ومن مشهد are two (elements) attached to ويل; and مشهد is a maṣdar mīmī, that is, "from their witnessing", in the sense of their presence; it is also permissible that it be a noun of time or place.
(أَسْمِعْ بِهِمْ وَأَبْصِرْ يَوْمَ يَأْتُونَنا لكِنِ الظَّالِمُونَ الْيَوْمَ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ): أسمع is a past verb that came in the form of the imperative, or it is indeclinable on an implied fatḥa on the silent last letter; and the bāʾ is a preposition added to the agent, which came as a pronoun in the accusative or genitive, for the appropriateness of the bāʾ. The discussion of wonder has preceded in detail, and the wonder here is directed to those addressed. لكن is the lightened (mukhaffafa) form, inoperative; والظالمون is a mubtadaʾ and في ضلال a khabar and مبين an adjective. He placed the overt noun in the place of the pronoun to signal that their wrongdoing reached the utmost and exceeded the limit. ويوم يأتوننا is attached to أسمع and أبصر.
(وَأَنْذِرْهُمْ يَوْمَ الْحَسْرَةِ إِذْ قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ وَهُمْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ): أنذرهم is an imperative verb, a latent agent and an object; ويوم الحسرة is an adverb attached to أنذرهم, but it is better that it be a direct object, that is, "make them fear the day itself". وإذ is attached to الحسرة, for a maṣdar made definite by al-, acts upon the explicit object, so how much more upon the adverb. It is also permissible that it be a badal from يوم الحسرة, so that it is governed by أنذر, and by that it is confirmed that يوم الحسرة is a direct object and not an adverb. وهم: the واو is circumstantial and هم is a mubtadaʾ and في غفلة a khabar; وهم لا يؤمنون is a ḥāl clause arranged together with the one before it. The two ḥāls are either from the latent pronoun in the words في ضلال مبين, that is, "they settled in manifest error in these two evil states", so the clause وأنذرهم would be parenthetical; or from the object in أنذرهم in these two evil states.
(إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَرِثُ الْأَرْضَ وَمَنْ عَلَيْها وَإِلَيْنا يُرْجَعُونَ): إن and its noun; and نحن is tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun نا, which has the meaning of نحن, because it has its meaning; the clause نرث الأرض is the khabar of إنا; ومن is conjoined to الأرض; وعليها are two (elements) attached to an omitted ṣila of من; وإلينا are two (elements) attached to يرجعون; and يرجعون is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil. In the wāw of the words وإلينا you may make it circumstantial or a conjunction.

* Rhetoric:
Al-majāz al-mursal (loose figurative usage) in the words «لكِنِ الظَّالِمُونَ الْيَوْمَ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ», the relationship being al-ḥāliyya (the contained for the container), and what is meant is Hell. So he used "the one that occupies" and meant "the place that is occupied", because error does not settle in it; rather it settles in its place. Likewise his words «وهم في غفلة»: heedlessness is not something one settles in either; rather one settles in the perils that cast their owners into heedlessness.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿آيَتُكَ أَلاَّ تُكَلِّمَ ٱلنَّاسَ ثَلاَثَ لَيَالٍ﴾ (your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights): (أن) is in the position of the nominative, i.e. your sign is this. (تُكَلِّمَ) is accusative by أن; and had it been made nominative (as He said: ﴿أَفَلاَ يَرْوَنَ إن لاَ يَرجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قُوْلاً:﴾ (do they not see that it does not return to them any speech?), it would have been correct.)
When you see the light أن with لا after it, test it with a pronoun such as hāʾ or kāf. If they fit, then both the nominative and the accusative are possible in the verb; if they do not fit, only the accusative is possible in the verb. Do you not see that it is permissible to say: آيَتك أنّك لا تكلّم الناس (your sign is that you will not speak to the people)? And that which can only be accusative is His saying: ﴿يُريدُ اللهُ أَلاّ يَجْعَلَ لَهُمْ حَظّاً﴾ (Allah intends not to give them any share), because the hāʾ is not suitable in (أن). So judge by these two «[Translator's note: the text has "على هلى هذين", evidently a dittography for على هذين.]».
His saying ﴿ثَلاَثَ لَيَالٍ سَوِيّاً﴾ (three nights, being sound): it is said: without dumbness.

farraa:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿فَأَوْحَىٰ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ (and he signalled to them): i.e. he pointed to them. The Arabs say أوحى إلىَّ, وَحّى, أومأ إلىَّ and وَمَى, with one meaning; and وَحَى يَحى and (وَمَى يَمِى); and "he signals to me with a signal (وَحْيا) that I do not understand".

farraa:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿وَحَنَاناً مِّن لَّدُنَّا﴾ (and affection from Us): الحَنَان is mercy. (He made حنانا accusative, i.e.) "and We did that as a mercy to his parents". (وَزَكَاةً) (and purity): he says: and righteousness. It is also said: and as a purification for them.

farraa:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿إِذِ ٱنتَبَذَتْ مِنْ أَهْلِهَا مَكَاناً شَرْقِياً﴾ (when she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east): it is said: in the eastern part of her family's house. The Arabs say: هو منى نَبْذَة and نُبْذَة (he is at some distance from me).

farraa:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿فَٱتَّخَذَتْ مِن دُونِهِم حِجَاباً﴾ (and she took a screen apart from them): when her menstruation came to her, she would put up a screen.

farraa:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿لأَهَبَ لَكِ﴾ (that I may grant you): the granting is from Allah; Gabriel related it to her as though he himself were the granter. That is frequent, in the Qurʾān especially. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (لِيَهَبَ لَكِ) (that He may grant you), and the meaning is: that Allah may grant you. As for the explanation of (لأهب لَكِ), it is like your saying: "He sent me with the word: 'that I may grant you'", as though he said: He said this: "that I may grant you", and the act belongs to Allah the Exalted.

farraa:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿ذِكْرُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ عَبْدَهُ زَكَرِيَّآ﴾ (a mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zechariah): الذكر is nominative by كهيعص (Kāf Hā Yā ʿAyn Ṣād). If you wish, you suppress (a subject): "this is a mention of the mercy of your Lord". The meaning is: your Lord's remembering His servant with His mercy; so there is fronting and postponement (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr). (زَكَرِيَّا) is in the position of the accusative.

farraa:47-48.t:
His saying: ﴿كَانَ بِي حَفِيّاً﴾: He was, towards me, knowing and gracious, answering my supplication when I call upon Him.
His saying: ﴿عَسَىۤ أَلاَّ أَكُونَ بِدُعَآءِ رَبِّي شَقِيّاً﴾: he is saying: if I call upon Him, I will not be made wretched by it.

farraa:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَمْ أَكُ بَغِيّاً﴾ (and I have not been unchaste): البَغِىّ is the dissolute woman.

farraa:50-50.t: His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُمْ لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ عَلِيّاً﴾: a goodly praise in every religion. Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām narrated to me from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtayba from Mujāhid, regarding His saying ﴿واجْعَل لِى لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ فىِ الآخِرِينَ﴾, he said: a goodly praise.

farraa:21-21.t: His saying: ﴿هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ﴾ (it is easy for Me): creating him is easy for Me.

farraa:52-52.t:
His saying: ﴿وَنَادَيْنَاهُ مِن جَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلأَيْمَنِ﴾ (of the mountain): the mountain (al-Ṭūr) has no right and no left; it is only the side that lies on your right, just as you say: "to the right of the qibla and to its left."
His saying ﴿وَقَرَّبْنَاهُ نَجِيّاً﴾: (it is a noun, not a maṣdar (verbal noun), but rather) it is like your saying mujālis and jalīs ("one who sits with someone"). Al-najiyy and al-najwā may each be both a noun and a maṣdar.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿مَكَاناً قَصِيّاً﴾ (a remote place): (قاصيا) has the same meaning. One of them recited to me:
لتقعُدِنَّ مَقعدَ القِصىّ * منى ذى القاذورةِ المقلىّ
(You shall sit, away from me, in the seat of the remote, the unclean, the hated one.)

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿وَكَانَ عِندَ رَبِّهِ مَرْضِيّاً﴾: had it come as marḍuwwan (مرضوّا), it would have been correct, because its root is with wāw; do you not see that al-riḍwān is with wāw? Those who said marḍiyyan built it on raḍītu (رضيت). (﴿ومَرْضُوّاً﴾ is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz.)

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأَجَآءَهَا ٱلْمَخَاضُ﴾ (and the pains of childbirth drove her): from جئت (to come), as you say: "the pains of childbirth came with her to the trunk of the palm tree". When you drop the bāʾ, you put an alif in the verb; as you say: آتيتكَ زيدا (I brought you Zayd), meaning أتيتك بزيد. Similar is ﴿آتُونِى زُبَرَ الحَدِيدِ﴾ (bring me sheets of iron): when you dropped the bāʾ you added an alif, and it is only ائتونى بزُبَر الحديد. There is another dialect form, not suitable in the Book, which is Tamīmī: فأشَاءَهَا المَخَاضُ. Among the proverbs of the Arabs: شرٌّ مَا ألجأك إلى مُخَّة عُرْقُوب (it was something bad that drove you to the marrow of a hock); the people of the Ḥijāz and the people of al-ʿĀliya say: شرّ مَا أجاءك إلى مُخَّة عرقوب, and the meaning is the same; and Tamīm say: شرّ مَا أشاءك إلى مُخَّة عرقوب.
His saying: ﴿وَكُنتُ نَسْياً﴾ (and had been a thing forgotten): [109a] «[Translator's note: "109 ا" is a manuscript folio marker.]» the companions of ʿAbd Allāh read نَسْيا with fatḥa on the nūn, and the rest of the Arabs give the nūn kasra; they are two dialect forms, like الجَسْر and الجِسْر (bridge), الحَجْر and الحِجْر, and الوَتْر and الوِتْر (odd number). النِّسْى is the rags of her impurity that a woman throws away (because when it is thrown away it is not taken back); it is اللَّقَى, with the short ending. It is النَّسْى; and had you meant by النَّسْى the maṣdar (verbal noun) of forgetting, it would have been correct — like your saying: حِجْرا محجوراً, i.e. حراما محرما (wholly forbidden), and نَسْيا مَنِسيّا (utterly forgotten). The Arabs say: نسيته نِسياناً and نسيا (I forgot it). One of them recited to me:
* من طاعة الربّ وعَصْى الشيطان *
(… out of obedience to the Lord and disobedience to Satan.)
He means: وعصيان الشيطان. Likewise أتيته إتيانا and أَتْياً (I came to him). The poet said:
أَتْىُ الفواحشِ فيهمُ معروفة * ويرون فعل المكرُمات حَرَامَا
(Committing indecencies is well known among them, and they regard doing noble deeds as forbidden.)

farraa:57-57.t: His saying: ﴿وَرَفَعْنَاهُ مَكَاناً عَلِيّاً﴾: it is related that Idrīs was [Translator's note: the text has «كا», evidently for «كان»] made beloved to the Angel of Death, so that he asked his Lord's permission to take him as a close friend. Then Idrīs asked the Angel of Death to show him the Fire; so he asked his Lord's permission and showed it to him. Then (he asked his Lord's permission) regarding Paradise, and showed it to him, and he entered it. The Angel of Death said to him: "Come out." He said: "By Allah, I will never come out of it, because Allah said ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إلاَّ وَارِدُهَا﴾, and I have already come down to it" — meaning the Fire — "and He said ﴿وَمَا هُمْ منها بِمُخْرَجِينَ﴾, so I will not come out of it except by His permission." So Allah said: "By My permission he entered it, so leave him." That is His saying ﴿وَرَفَعْنَاه مَكَاناً عَلِيّاً﴾.

farraa:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِن تَحْتِهَآ﴾ (then he called her from beneath her) and ﴿نَادَاهَا مِن تَحْتَهَآ﴾ (the one beneath her called her): it is the angel in both aspects alike, i.e. Gabriel called her from beneath her; and "the one beneath her called her": the one who was beneath her. His saying (سَرِيّاً): السرِىّ is a stream.

farraa:59-59.t: His saying: ﴿فَخَلَفَ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ﴾ khalf: khalf (with sukūn) is taken in the sense of blame, while khalaf (with fatḥa) is the righteous successor. Yet khalaf may occur for the bad and khalf for the righteous, because they sometimes take khalf to mean one generation after another.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿وَهُزِّىۤ إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ ٱلنَّخْلَةِ﴾ (and shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree): the Arabs say هَزَّ بهِ and هزَّه (he shook it), خذ الخِطَام and خذ بالخِطَام (take the halter), تعلَّق زيدا and تعلَّق بزيد (cling to Zayd), خُذْ برأسه and خذ رأسه (take his head), and امدد بالحبل (and امدد الحبلَ) (stretch the rope). Allah said ﴿فَلْيَمْدُدْ بِسَبَبٍ إلى السَّمَاءِ﴾ (let him extend a rope to the ceiling); its meaning is: let him extend a rope (to the sky). Likewise in His saying ﴿وَهُزِّىۤ إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ ٱلنَّخْلَةِ﴾, had it been وهُزّى جذعَ النخلة, it would have been correct.
His saying: ﴿يَسَّاقط﴾ (it will drop): it is also read ﴿تُسَاقِطْ عَلَيْكِ﴾, and تَسَاقط and تُسَاقِط (with tāʾ). Whoever read it يَسَّاقط referred it to the trunk. Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib read it with yāʾ, and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh (تساقط), meaning the palm; you may make it doubled if you wish, or light if you wish. And if you say ﴿تُسَاقِط عَلَيك﴾, it is correct. Doubled and light forms are both possible in the one beginning with tāʾ, while the doubled form alone is possible in the one beginning with yāʾ. Had a reader read تُسْقِط عليك رطبا (it will drop fresh dates on you), referring to the palm, or said يَسْقط عَليكِ رُطَباً, referring to the trunk, it would have been correct.
His saying (جَنِيّاً) (ripe): الجَنِىّ and المَجْنِىّ (picked) are one; it is (in sense) a passive participle (mafʿūl bihi).

farraa:61-61.t:
His saying: ﴿جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ﴾ is accusative (manṣūb). Had you put it in the nominative as a new beginning (istiʾnāf), it would have been correct.
His saying ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ وَعْدُهُ مَأْتِيّاً﴾: and He did not say ātiyan ("coming"). Everything that comes to you, you also come to it; do you not see that you say "I have come upon fifty years" and "fifty years have come upon me"? All of that is correct.

farraa:26-26.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَرِّي عَيْناً﴾ (and be content [lit. cool of eye]): it has come in the commentary: be of good cheer. "The eye" was made accusative only because the verb was originally its own, and you transferred it to the woman. Its meaning is: let your eye be cooled. When the verb is transferred from its owner to what precedes it, the owner of the verb is made accusative as an explanation (tafsīr, i.e. tamyīz (specification)). Similar is ﴿فَإنْ طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ شِىْءٍ مِنْهُ نَفساً﴾ (but if they willingly give up to you anything of it), whose meaning is only: if their souls are pleased «[Translator's note: the text has "طالت"; طابت is evidently meant.]» for you; and ضاق به ذَرْعاً and ضِقت به ذَرْعاً (he/I was distressed by it), and سؤت به ظَنّاً (I thought ill of him), which only (means: my opinion of him was bad). Likewise مررت برَجل حسنٍ وجهاً (I passed by a man handsome of face), whose meaning was only: his face was handsome; you transferred the verb of the face to the man, so "face" became the specifier. Build on this whatever you wish. His saying: ﴿إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ صَوْماً﴾ (indeed I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast): i.e. silence.

farraa:62-62.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَهُمْ رِزْقُهُمْ فِيهَا بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيّاً﴾: there is no morning and no evening there, but they are brought their provision according to the measures of morning and evening in this world.

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتِ شَيْئاً فَرِيّاً﴾ (you have certainly done a thing unprecedented): الفرِىّ is a tremendous matter. The Arabs say: يَفْرِى الفَرِىّ (he does marvels) when someone does excellent work, or (excellent) watering, and surpasses people; this is said of him. The rajaz poet said:
قد أَطعمتنْى دَقَلاً حَجْرِيّاً * قد كنت تفرين به الفَرِيَّا
(You have fed me poor dates from Ḥajr — dates with which you used to do marvels.)
i.e. you used to eat them in great quantity.

farraa:64-64.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا نَتَنَزَّلُ إِلاَّ بِأَمْرِ رَبِّكَ﴾ means the angels. And His saying: to Him belongs ﴿مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِينَا﴾ of the affair of this world, ﴿وَمَا خَلْفَنَا﴾ of the affair of the Hereafter, ﴿وَمَا بَيْنَ ذٰلِكَ﴾: it is said: what is between the two blasts (of the Trumpet), and between them are forty years.

farraa:28-28.t: His saying: ﴿يٰأُخْتَ هَارُونَ﴾ (O sister of Aaron): she had a brother called Aaron, one of the best of the Children of Israel, who was not from her parents; so it was said: O sister of Aaron in his righteousness. I.e. your brother is righteous and your parents are (well-known) parents — as a reproach to her; i.e. the people of your house are righteous, and you have committed a grave thing.

farraa:66-66.t: His saying: ﴿لَسَوْفَ أُخْرَجُ حَيّاً﴾ and (أُخْرُجُ) are two readings.

farraa:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ﴾ (so she pointed to him): to her son. It is said that the cradle (المهد) was her lap — حِجْرها and حَجْرها. It is also said: his bed. "Lap" is better.

farraa:67-67.t: His saying: ﴿أَوَلاَ يَذْكُرُ ٱلإِنْسَٰنُ﴾: in the reading of Ubayy it is (يَتَذَكَّرُ), while the readers — ʿĀṣim and others — have read (يَذْكُرُ).

farraa:31-32.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَنِي مُبَارَكاً﴾ (and He has made me blessed): one from whom people learn wherever I am.
His saying: ﴿جَبَّاراً﴾ (a tyrant): الجبّار is one who kills in anger and strikes in anger.
His saying ﴿وَبَرّاً بِوَالِدَتِي﴾ (and dutiful to my mother): you make it accusative on the basis of "He made me a prophet, and made me dutiful", following on from "prophet"; as in His saying (وَجَزَاهُمْ بِمَا صَبَرُوا جَنَّةً وحَرِيراً) (and He will reward them for their patience with a garden and silk), then He said ﴿وَدَانِيَةً عَلَيهِمْ ظِلاَلُهَا﴾ (and near above them are its shades): (دانيةً) refers back to ﴿مُتَّكِئين فيهَا﴾ (reclining therein), just as البَرّ refers back to His saying ﴿نَبِيّاً﴾ (a prophet).

farraa:73-73.t: His saying: ﴿خَيْرٌ مَّقَاماً وَأَحْسَنُ نَدِيّاً﴾: an assembly (majlis). Al-nadiyy and al-nādī are two dialectal forms.

farraa:33-33.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيَّ﴾ (and peace is on me): it has come in the commentary: safety is upon me.

farraa:74-74.t: His saying: ﴿أَحْسَنُ أَثَاثاً وَرِءْياً﴾: al-athāth is household goods (al-matāʿ), and al-riʾy is outward appearance. Al-athāth has no singular, just as al-matāʿ has no singular. The Arabs pluralize al-matāʿ as amtiʿa, amātīʿ and mutuʿ. Were you to pluralize al-athāth, you would say "three āththa", and uthath, nothing else. The people of Medina read it without hamza (وَرِيّاً), and that is a good option, because it comes with verses whose endings are not hamzated. It is also reported of some of them that they took al-riyy to be from rawītu ("I quenched my thirst"). Some read it (وَزِيّاً) with zāy; al-ziyy is form and appearance. The Arabs say: "qad zayyaytu the slave girl", i.e. I adorned her and dressed her up.

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying: ﴿قَوْلَ ٱلْحَقِّ﴾ (the word of truth): in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (قالُ اللّهِ الحقُّ) (the word of Allah, the Truth); القول and القال have one meaning.
"The Truth" in this place means Allah. Had "the true word" been meant by it, with القول put in construct with الحقّ while meaning "the true word", it would have been correct, as it is said: ﴿إنَّ هَذَا لَهُوَ حَقُّ اليَقِين﴾ (indeed this is the truth of certainty), a thing being put in construct with its like. Similar is the saying of Allah ﴿وَعْدَ الصِّدْقِ الَّذِى كانُوا يُوعَدُونَ﴾ (the promise of truth which they had been promised), whose meaning is the true promise. Likewise ﴿ولَدَارُ الآخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ﴾ (and the home of the Hereafter is better), which is only: والدار الآخرةُ.
The readers have read with the accusative (قَوْلَ الحقّ), and it is common, meaning by it: truly (حَقّاً). And if you make القول accusative while intending it (to refer to) a description of Jesus, it would be correct, as though you said: هذا عبدالله أخاه بعينه (this is ʿAbd Allāh, his very brother). The Arabs make the definite noun accusative in (sentences with) هذا, ذلك and their sisters; so they say: هذا عبدالله الأَسَدَ عادياً (this is ʿAbd Allāh, the lion, attacking), just as they say: أسداً عاديا (a lion, attacking).

farraa:76-76.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَزِيدُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱهْتَدَواْ هُدًى﴾: through the abrogating and the abrogated.

farraa:35-35.t: His saying: ﴿مَا كَانَ للَّهِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ مِن وَلَدٍ﴾ (it is not [befitting] for Allah to take a son): (أن) is in the position of the nominative.

farraa:77-77.t:
His saying: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي﴾: without hamza.

His saying: ﴿لأُوتَيَنَّ مَالاً وَوَلَداً﴾: Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: al-Mughīra narrated to me from Ibrāhīm that he used to read (مَالُهُ وَوُلْدُهُ), and in Kāf-Hā-Yā-ʿAyn-Ṣād [Translator's note: i.e. Sūrat Maryam] (مَالاً ووُلْداً). Al-Farrāʾ said: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read likewise. ʿĀṣim gave the wāw a fatḥa, and read it with full vowels throughout the whole Qurʾān. Mujāhid read (مالُه ووُلْدُه إلاَّ خَسَاراً) [Translator's note: Sūrat Nūḥ 71:21] in the nominative, with fatḥa in the rest of the Qurʾān. The poet said:
ولقد رأيت معاشرا * قد ثَمّروا مَالاً ووُلْدَا
(I have seen groups of people who had made wealth and offspring grow.)
He used the light form [Translator's note: the parenthesis in the source reads «(وثَمروا)»; the light form meant is evidently وُلْد]. Al-wuld and al-walad are two dialectal forms, like (what they said): al-ʿadam and al-ʿudm (and al-wuld and al-walad), and they are one and the same (and not a plural). Among the proverbs of the Arabs: "وُلْدُكِ مَن دَمَّى عقبيكِ" (your child is the one who bloodied your heels). And one of the poets said:
فليت فلاناً مات فى بطن أمّه * وليت فلانا كان وُلْدَ حمار
(Would that so-and-so had died in his mother's belly, and would that so-and-so had been the offspring of a donkey.)
So this is a singular. Qays make al-wuld a plural and al-walad a singular.

farraa:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ﴾ (and indeed Allah): it is also read ﴿وأَنَّ اللهَ﴾. Whoever reads it with fatḥa means: that is (because) Allah is my Lord and your Lord. It may be nominative, and it may be (in interpretation) genitive, on the basis of "and because Allah", as He said ﴿ذَلِكَ أَنْ لَمْ يكُنْ رَبكَ مُهْلِكَ القُرَى بِظُلْمٍ﴾ (that is because your Lord would not destroy the towns for wrongdoing). Had you given (أنَّ) fatḥa on the basis of His saying ﴿وَأَوْصَانىِ بِالصَّلاَةِ والزكاةِ﴾ (and He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakāh) — (and that Allah…) — it would be a valid aspect. In the reading of Ubayy: (إِن الله ربّى وربّكم) without the wāw, and this is evidence that it has kasra.

farraa:80-80.t: His saying: ﴿وَنَرِثُهُ مَا يَقُولُ﴾ means: what al-ʿĀṣī ibn Wāʾil claims he will have in Paradise, so We give it to someone else. ﴿وَيَأْتِينَا فَرْداً﴾: devoid of wealth and children.

farraa:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَمْ أَكُنْ بِدُعَآئِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيّاً﴾ (and never have I been, in my supplication to You, my Lord, unhappy): he says: I have not been made wretched by calling on You; You answered me when I called You.

farraa:81-81.t: His saying: ﴿لِّيَكُونُواْ لَهُمْ عِزّاً﴾: He is saying: so that they might be intercessors for them in the Hereafter.

farraa:82-82.t: So Allah said: ﴿كَلاَّ سَيَكْفُرُونَ بِعِبَادَتِهِمْ وَيَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضِدّاً﴾: they will be helpers against them.

farraa:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱذْكُرْ فِي ٱلْكِتَابِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ (and mention in the Book Abraham): relate the story of Abraham; recite it to them. Likewise His saying regarding the prophets He mentioned, (i.e.) relate to them their stories.

farraa:83-83.t: His saying: ﴿أَنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا ٱلشَّيَاطِينَ عَلَى ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾ (in this world) ﴿تَؤُزُّهُمْ أَزّاً﴾: they agitate them towards acts of disobedience and incite them to them.

farraa:45-45.t: His saying: ﴿إِنِّيۤ أَخَافُ أَن يَمَسَّكَ عَذَابٌ﴾ (indeed I fear that a punishment will touch you): He means: I know. It is like His saying ﴿فَخَشِينَا أَنْ يُرْهِقَهُمَا﴾ (and we feared that he would overburden them), i.e. and we knew.

farraa:84-84.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّمَا نَعُدُّ لَهُمْ عَدّاً﴾: it is said: the days, the nights, the months and the years. Some of the exegetes said: the breaths.

farraa:46-46.t:
His saying: ﴿لأَرْجُمَنَّكَ﴾ (I will surely stone you): I will surely revile you.
His saying: ﴿وَٱهْجُرْنِي مَلِيّاً﴾ (and leave me for a long while): a long time. One says: I was with him مَلْوةً of time, and مُلْوةً, مِلْوةً and مُلاَوَةً of time. Hudhayl say مِلاوة, and some Arabs مَلاوة. All of it is from length.

farraa:85-85.t: His saying: ﴿نَحْشُرُ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ إِلَى ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ وَفْداً﴾: al-wafd is riders (on mounts).

farraa:5-5.t: His saying: ﴿ٱلْمَوَالِيَ﴾ (the kinsmen): they are a man's (paternal cousins) and his heirs. الوَلِىّ and المَوْلى are one in the speech of the Arabs; in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (إنَّمَا مَوْلاَكُمُ اللهُ ورَسُولَهُ) (your patron is only Allah and His Messenger) in place of (وَليُّكُمْ). It was mentioned regarding (the reading) خَفَّتِ الموالى (the kinsmen have become few) that it means "they became few"; it was reported from ʿUthmān (ibn ʿAffān).

farraa:86-86.t: His saying: ﴿وَنَسُوقُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ وِرْداً﴾: on foot and thirsty.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿يَرِثُنِي﴾ (who will inherit from me): it is read in the jussive and in the nominative. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it in the jussive, and the jussive is the (preferred) aspect, because (يرثنى) is in a verse other than the first, so the conditional answer (jazāʾ) is good. When you make it nominative, it is a ṣila (qualifying clause) of "the heir": "grant me one who will inherit from me". Similar are ﴿رِدْءًا يُصَدِّقُنِى﴾ (as a helper, confirming me) and ﴿يُصَدِّقْنِى﴾.
When you make an imperative fall upon an indefinite noun followed by a verb beginning with yāʾ, tāʾ, nūn or alif, there are two aspects in it: the jussive, as the answer of the condition; and the nominative, as a qualifying clause of the indefinite noun, in the role of الذى (who/which). As someone says: أعِرنى دابَّة أركبْها (lend me a mount and I will ride it) or, if you wish, أركبُها (a mount that I may ride). Likewise ﴿أَنْزِلْ علَيْنَا مَائِدَةً مِنَ السَّمَاءِ تَكُونُ لَنَا﴾ (send down to us a table from heaven to be for us); had He said (تَكُنْ لَنَا), it would have been correct. But when the verb after the indefinite noun does not pertain to the first (noun), and suppressing the hāʾ (pronoun) is not suitable in it — if the verb falls on the man — then only the jussive is possible; as you say: هَبْ لى ثوباً أَتَجَمَّل مع الناس (give me a garment, and I will look fine among people): (أتجمَّل) can only be jussive, because the hāʾ is not suitable in أتجمّل. And you say: أَعِرنى دابَّة أركبُ يا هذا (lend me a mount I may ride, you there), because you could say أركبُها, suppressing the hāʾ, so that is fitting.

farraa:87-87.t: His saying: ﴿لاَّ يَمْلِكُونَ ٱلشَّفَاعَةَ﴾: they will not have the power to intercede, ﴿إِلاَّ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ عِندَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ عَهْداً﴾: and the covenant is "There is no god but Allah". (مَن) is in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as the excepted (mustathnā); it cannot be genitive by an implied lām, but it is accusative carrying the sense of the genitive, just as you say in speech: "I wanted to pass by today, except the enemy, for I will not pass by him" — you except him according to the meaning; and had you made the bāʾ overt and said "I wanted to pass by, except by the enemy", you would have put it in the genitive. Likewise if it were said: "They will not have the power of intercession except for one who has taken with the Most Merciful [110 b] a covenant."

farraa:7-8.t:
His saying: ﴿لَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيّاً﴾ (We have not assigned to any before this name): no one was named Yaḥyā before Yaḥyā son of Zechariah.
His saying: ﴿مِنَ ٱلْكِبَرِ عِتِيّاً﴾ (extreme old age) and (عِتيّا): Ibn ʿAbbās read (عُسِيّاً). You say of an old man when he has aged: قد عَتَا and عَسَا (he has become withered), as is said of a stick when it dries up.

farraa:89-89.t: His saying: ﴿ لَّقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْئاً إِدّاً﴾: the readers read it with kasra on the alif, except Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, who read it with fatḥa (أَدّا). Some of the Arabs say: "You have brought something āddin (آدٍّ)", like māddin (مادّ). In all of its forms it means: something enormous.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿قَالَ كَذٰلِكَ قَالَ رَبُّكَ هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ﴾ (he said: "Thus [it will be]; your Lord says: It is easy for Me"): i.e. creating him is easy for Me.

farraa:90-90.t:
His saying: ﴿وَتَخِرُّ ٱلْجِبَالُ هَدّاً﴾: breaking apart.
His saying: ﴿يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنْهُ﴾, and yanfaṭirna. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is (إن تكاد السَّموات لتتصَدَّع منه), and Ḥamza read it (يَنْفَطِرْنَ) in this sense.

farraa:91-91.t: His saying: ﴿أَن دَعَوْا﴾: because they ascribed, and for having ascribed. The position of (أَن) is accusative because of its being joined [Translator's note: i.e. joined directly to what precedes once the preposition is dropped]. Al-Kisāʾī used to say: (the position of أن) is genitive.

farraa:93-93.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ آتِي ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ عَبْداً﴾: had you said "ātin al-Raḥmāna ʿabdan" (آتٍ الرحمن, with tanwīn and the accusative), it would have been correct, but I have not heard it from any reader.

farraa:96-96.t: His saying: ﴿وُدّاً﴾: Allah places love for them in the hearts of the believers.

farraa:98-98.t: His saying: ﴿أَوْ تَسْمَعُ لَهُمْ رِكْزاً﴾: al-rikz is a sound.

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: (ووهبنا لهم من رحمتنا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The two preposition and its genitive nouns are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the preposition and its genitive noun «لهم» is attached to the second object. «عليًّا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «لسان».

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: The clause «إنه كان» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of Moses. «نبيًا» is a second khabar (predicate) of «كان».

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: The clause «وناديناه» is conjoined to the clause {وَكَانَ رَسُولا}; «نجيا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: (ووهبنا له من رحمتنا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The two preposition and its genitive nouns are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; «هارون» is a badal (substitute), and «نبيا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «أخاه».

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: The clause «إنه كان» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «إسماعيل».

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: «عند»: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of kāna, «مرضيًا».

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: The clause «إنه كان» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «إدريس».

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: «مكانا» is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause «ورفعناه» is conjoined to the clause {إِنَّهُ كَانَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: «الذين» is a badal (substitute) of the relative noun; the preposition and its genitive noun «من النبيين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «عليهم», and the second preposition and its genitive noun is a badal of the first. The preposition and its genitive noun «وممَّن» is conjoined to «من ذرية» and is attached to what that is attached to. The conditional clause is the khabar (predicate) of «أولئك», and His saying «سجَّدا» is a ḥāl of the wāw.

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: The clause «فخلف» is resumptive, the clause «أضاعوا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «خلف», and the clause «فسوف يلقون» is conjoined to the clause «اتبعوا».

harrat-mujtaba:60-60.t: «من» is a relative noun, accusative (manṣūb) as the excepted (in exception); «صالحًا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «فأولئك يدخلون» is resumptive. «شيئا» is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: they will not be wronged with any wrong, little or much.

harrat-mujtaba:61-61.t: «جنات» is a badal (substitute) of {الْجَنَّةَ}, and «عدن» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The relative noun is a naʿt (adjective) of «جنات», and the preposition and its genitive noun «بالغيب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the relative's referent pronoun in «وعدها», i.e.: while it is unseen by them. The clause «إنه كان وعده مأتيا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:62-62.t: The clause «لا يسمعون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «جنات عدن»; «سلامًا» is a disconnected excepted (mustathnā munqaṭiʿ). The clause «ولهم رزقُهم» is conjoined to the clause «لا يسمعون». «بكرة» is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the aforementioned "being established" (istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) of «رزقهم» is attached.

harrat-mujtaba:63-63.t: «تلك الجنة»: mubtadaʾ (subject) and badal (substitute); the relative noun is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. The preposition and its genitive noun «من عبادنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the «مَنْ» that follows.

harrat-mujtaba:64-64.t: The clause «وما نتنزل» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «بأمر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. «بين» is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) attached to the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause), and the clause «له ما بين أيدينا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ربك».

harrat-mujtaba:65-65.t: «رب» is a badal (substitute) of {رَبِّكَ}; the clause «فاعبدْه» is resumptive, and so is the clause «هل تعلم».

harrat-mujtaba:66-66.t: The clause «ويقول» is resumptive. «ما» after «إذا» is redundant (zāʾida), and «إذا» is a conditional adverb (ẓarfiyya sharṭiyya) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied (muqaddar) verb indicated by His saying «لسوف أُخْرَج», its implied form being: when I die, shall I be resurrected; it is not attached to «أخرج», because what comes after the lām does not govern what precedes it. The clause «لسوف أخرج» is explicative of the implied verb, and the lām is for emphasis (tawkīd).

harrat-mujtaba:67-67.t: The clause «أوَلا يَذْكر» is conjoined to the earlier clause «يقول الإنسان», and the maṣdar «أنَّا خلقناه» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «ولم يك» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in «خلقناه». «يك» is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) with the sukūn implied (muqaddar) on the nūn, which was dropped for lightness.

harrat-mujtaba:68-68.t: His saying «فَوَرَبِّك»: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the wāw is a particle of oath and a preposition; «ربك» is a genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted "I swear" (أقسم). «الشياطين» is a noun conjoined to the hāʾ, and «جثيا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:69-69.t: His saying «أيُّهم أشد»: a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «أشد» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: هو, and the clause «هو أشد» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عِتِيًّا», and «عِتِيًّا» is tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:70-70.t: His saying «لنحن»: the lām occurs in the response to the preceding oath; the preposition and its genitive noun «بها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أولى»; «صِلِيًّا» is tamyīz (specification). The clause «ثم لنحن أعلم» is conjoined to the clause «ننزعَنَّ».

harrat-mujtaba:71-71.t: The wāw is resumptive and «إنْ» is negating; the preposition and its genitive noun «منكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an adjective of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: وإن أحد كائن منكم (and there is no one, being from among you,); «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr), and «واردها» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. The clause «كان» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:73-73.t: The conditional clause is resumptive. «أيُّ» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and «خير» is the khabar (predicate); «مقامًا» is tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:74-74.t: «كم» is the predicative (khabariyya) kam, an object placed first; the preposition and its genitive noun «من قرن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an adjective of «كَمْ». The clause «هم أحسن» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قرن», and the pronoun is made plural by construing it according to its meaning. «أثاثا» is tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:75-75.t: «من»: a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition and its genitive noun «في الضَّلالة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). The clause «فلْيَمْدُد» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the lām is the lām of command which puts the verb in the jussive. «حتى» is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya), and the conditional clause is resumptive. «ما» is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «إمَّا» is a particle of detailing (tafṣīl); «العذاب» is a badal (substitute) of «ما»; the clause «فسيعلمون» is the apodosis; «مكانًا» is tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:76-76.t: The two objects of «يزيد» are the relative noun and «هدى». The clause «يزيد» is resumptive, and the clause «والباقيات الصالحات خير» is conjoined to the resumptive one.

harrat-mujtaba:77-77.t: His saying «أفرأيت»: the hamza is for interrogation and the fāʾ is resumptive. The oath clause with its response is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb), and the clause «لأوتَيَنَّ» is the answer to the oath; «مالا» is the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:78-78.t: «الغيب» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), from their saying «اطَّلَعَ فُلانٌ الجبلَ», i.e. he climbed to its top. «أم» is a conjunction, and the clause «أَطَّلَع» is the second object of «أرأيت».

harrat-mujtaba:79-79.t: «كلا» is a particle of deterrence and rebuke (radʿ wa-zajr); «ما» is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «مدًا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the two preposition and its genitive nouns are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نَمُدَّ».

harrat-mujtaba:80-80.t: «ما» is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) of the pronoun in «نَرِثُه», and «فَرْدًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun «نا».

harrat-mujtaba:81-81.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «من دون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object; the preposition and its genitive noun «لهم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «عِزًّا».

harrat-mujtaba:82-82.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «عليهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ضِدًّا». «ضدًّا» was made singular even though it is a khabar (predicate) about a plural, because it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the maṣdar is singular and masculine.

harrat-mujtaba:83-83.t: (ألم تر أنا أرسلنا الشياطين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The interpreted maṣdar stands in place of the two objects of raʾā, and the clause «تَؤُزُّهُم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الشياطين».

harrat-mujtaba:84-84.t: The clause «فلا تَعْجَل» is conjoined to the clause {أَرْسَلْنَا}.

harrat-mujtaba:85-85.t: «يوم» is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) {نَعُدُّ}; «وفدًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «المتقين».

harrat-mujtaba:87-87.t: The clause «لا يملكون» is a second ḥāl (circumstantial) of {الْمُجْرِمِينَ}. «مَن» is a relative noun, excepted; the adverb «عند» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted second object.

harrat-mujtaba:88-88.t: The first object of «اتخذ» is implied (muqaddar), i.e.: Jesus.

harrat-mujtaba:89-89.t: (لقد جئتم شيئا إدا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The oath with its response is a resumptive clause; «إدًّا» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:90-90.t: «هَدًّا» is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and it is synonymous in meaning with the word governing it.

harrat-mujtaba:91-91.t: «أن» is a maṣdar-forming particle, and the interpreted maṣdar is accusative by removal of the preposition: the lām.

harrat-mujtaba:92-92.t: The clause «وما ينبغي» is resumptive; the interpreted maṣdar is the fāʿil (agent) of «ينبغي», and the verb «ينبغي» is made transitive with the lām.

harrat-mujtaba:93-93.t: «إن» is negating; «كل» is mubtadaʾ (subject); «مَن» is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); «آتي» is the khabar (predicate) of «كل»; «عبدا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «آتي», and the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:94-94.t: The clause «لقد أحصاهم» is the answer to the oath, and the oath with its response is a resumptive clause.

harrat-mujtaba:95-95.t: The clause «وكلهم آتيه» is conjoined to the preceding answer to the oath; «فردا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «آتيه».

harrat-mujtaba:96-96.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) second object of jaʿala.

harrat-mujtaba:97-97.t: The clause «فإنما يسَّرناه» is resumptive, and the genitive maṣdar «لتبشِّر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يسَّرناه».

harrat-mujtaba:98-98.t: His saying «وكم»: the wāw is resumptive; «كم» is the predicative (khabariyya) kam, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first, and the preposition and its genitive noun «من قرن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an adjective of «كم». The clause «هل تحس» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «منهم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «أحد», and the second «مِن» is redundant (zāʾida); «أحد» is the object of «تحس».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: His words «ذكر رحمة ربك عبده زكريا»: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: هذا (this). «عبده» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the maṣdar (verbal noun) «رحمة»; «زكريا» is a badal (substitute) of «عبده».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «إذ نادى»: an adverbial noun, a badal (substitute) of inclusion (ishtimāl), and the clause «نادى» is muḍāf ilayhi.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «ربِّ»: one addressed in the vocative, in construct, accusative with a fatḥa implied on the letter before the dropped yāʾ. The preposition «مني» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «العظم». «شيبًا» is a tamyīz (specification) converted from the fāʿil (agent), i.e.: واشتعل شيبُ الرأس (and the grey hair of the head blazed). The preposition «بدعائك» is attached to the khabar (predicate). The clause «ربِّ» is parenthetical between the noun of كان and its khabar, and the preposition «بدعائك» is attached to «شقيا».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The preposition «من ورائي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الموالي»; the clause «وكانت» is a ḥāl of the tāʾ in «خفت»; and the clause «فهب» is conjoined to the clause «إني خفت».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «يرثني» is a naʿt (adjective) of {وَلِيًّا}, and the clause «رب» is parenthetical between the two objects of «جعل».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «اسمه يحيى» is a naʿt (adjective) of «غلام», and likewise the clause «لم نجعل» is a second naʿt of «غلام». The preposition «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object; the preposition «من قبل» is attached to «نجعل».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: «أنى»: an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the preposition «لي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); «غلام» is the noun of كان; the clause «وكانت» is a ḥāl of the yāʾ in «لي»; and the preposition «من الكبر» is attached to a ḥāl of «عتيا».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: His words «كذلك»: the kāf is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: الأمر كذلك (the matter is thus), and the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi. The preposition «عليَّ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar «هينٌ». The clause «وقد خلقتك» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the yāʾ in «عليَّ», and the clause «ولم تك» is conjoined to the circumstantial one. His words «تك»: a defective imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) with a sukūn implied on the dropped nūn.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The preposition «لي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object. The maṣdar (verbal noun) «ألا تكلم» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject); «ثلاث» is an adverb attached to «تكلم»; «سويًّا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «تكلم».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: (على قومه من المحراب) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The two preposition and its genitive nouns are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خرج», and «أنْ» is explicative (tafsīriyya). The clause «سبِّحوا» is explicative; «بكرة» is an adverb of time attached to the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The preposition «بقوة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «خذ». The clause «وآتيناه» is resumptive; «صبيا» is a ḥāl of the hāʾ. The clause «يا يحيى» is what is said (maqūl al-qawl) by an implied resumptive saying, i.e.: Allah said: O Yaḥyā.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: «وحنانًا»: a noun conjoined to {الْحُكْمَ}, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «حنانًا». The clause «وكان» is conjoined to the clause «آتيناه».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: His words «وبَرًّا»: a noun conjoined to {تَقِيًّا}, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «برًّا»; «عصيا» is a second khabar (predicate) of كان.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: His words «وسلام»: the wāw is a conjunction; «سلام» is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and «عليه» the khabar (predicate); beginning with an indefinite is permitted because it indicates a supplication. The clause «وسلام عليه» is conjoined to the clause «لم يكن». «يوم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [notion of] being settled (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached. «حيا»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «يبعث».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The clause «واذكر» is resumptive; «إذ» is an adverbial noun, a badal (substitute) of inclusion (ishtimāl) from «مريم»; «مكانًا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and [what follows is] its naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «فاتخذت» is conjoined to the clause {انْتَبَذَتْ}; the preposition (مِنْ دُونِهِمْ) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object. «سويا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «بشرًا».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The preposition «منك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أعوذ». The clause «إن كنت» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The genitive maṣdar (verbal noun) «لأهب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «رسول».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: «أنى»: an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the preposition «لي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); the clause «ولم يمسسني بشر» is a ḥāl of the yāʾ in «لي»; and the clause «ولم أك» is conjoined to the circumstantial clause.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: His words «كذلك»: the kāf is a noun in the sense of مثل (like), the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: الأمر مثل ذلك (the matter is like that). The second clause «قال» is resumptive. The preposition «منا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of رحمة. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is attached to an omitted verb, i.e.: خلقناه كذلك لنجعله (We created him thus that We might make him), and the implied clause is conjoined to the clause «هو عليَّ هين».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The preposition «به» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «انتبذت»; «مكانًا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: His words «أجاءها» contain the sense of ألجأها (drove her), and the clause is conjoined to the clause «انتبذت». «يا» is a particle for drawing attention (tanbīh).

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: «أن» is explicative (tafsīriyya), and the clause after it is explicative. The clause «قد جعل» is resumptive within the scope of the explanation. The adverb «تحتك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «جعل».

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The preposition «إليك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being: أعني إليك (I mean: towards you). It may not be attached to «هُزِّي», because the verb of a connected pronoun does not pass over to its own connected pronoun outside the chapter of ظن and فقد; so one does not say: فرحتُ بي (I rejoiced in me) or ضربتُني (I struck me). The preposition «بجذع» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of «هُزِّي», i.e.: shake the fresh dates, being on a trunk. The verb «تساقط» is jussive (majzūm), because it occurs as the apodosis of an implied condition.

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: His words «فإما ترَيِنَّ»: the fāʾ is a conjunction, «إن» is conditional, «ما» is redundant (zāʾida), and the imperfect verb is jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn. Its original form before emphasis was تَرْأَيِِين: the kasra on the yāʾ was felt heavy and was dropped, so two quiescent letters met, and the final radical (lām al-kalima) was dropped, so it became تَرْأَيْن; the vowel of the hamza was transferred to the rāʾ, then the hamza was dropped for lightening, so it became تَرَيْن; then the jussive particle entered and the nūn of the nominative was dropped, so it became تَرَيْ; then it was emphasised with the nūn, so two quiescent letters met, and the yāʾ was given the vowel that suits it, the kasra, so it became تَرَيِنَّ. It is thus an imperfect verb, jussive by the dropping of the nūn; the yāʾ is the fāʿil (agent), and the nūn is for emphasis. The preposition «من البشر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «أحدًا». The clause «فلن أكلم» is conjoined to the clause «نذرْتُ».

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «تحمله» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «أتت». The clause «يا مريمُ لقد جئت» is what is said (maqūl al-qawl); the clause of the oath with its apodosis is the response to the vocative, resumptive; and the clause «لقد جئت» is the apodosis of the oath.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: «كيف»: an interrogative noun, ḥāl (circumstantial); the preposition «في المهد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl of «صبيا».

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The clause «آتاني» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the noun of «إن»; «نبيًا» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: «أينما»: a conditional noun, an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) كنت; «ما» is redundant (zāʾida); «كنت» is a complete past verb with its fāʿil (agent). «ما دمت»: «ما» is a temporal maṣdariyya, and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is an adverb of time attached to «أوصاني». The clause «أين ما كنت» is parenthetical between the two conjoined elements, and the clause «وَأَوْصَانِي» is conjoined to the clause «جعلني». The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: «برا»: conjoined to {مُبَارَكًا}, and the preposition «بوالدتي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «برًّا». The clause «لم يجعلني» is conjoined to the earlier clause «جعلني».

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The clause «والسلام عليَّ» is conjoined to the clause «لم يجعلني». «يوم» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [notion of] being settled (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached; «حيا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: «قول»: a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is implied, i.e.: أقول قول (I say a saying); the implied clause أقول is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يتخذ» is the noun of كان; the preposition «لله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of كان. The first object of «يتخذ» is implied, i.e.: أحدا (anyone), and «ولد» is the second object, «مِن» being redundant (zāʾida). «سبحانه» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). «إذا» is a conditional adverb attached to the sense of the apodosis, and the conditional clause is resumptive. The clause «يكون» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: فهو يكون; and the clause «فهو يكون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The clause «فاعبدوه» is conjoined to the clause «إن الله ربي». The clause «وإن الله ربي» is what is said (maqūl al-qawl) by an implied resumptive saying, and the clause «هذا صراط» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: His words «فويل للذين»: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «ويل» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); beginning with an indefinite is permitted because it indicates a supplication. The clause «فويل للذين» is conjoined to the preceding resumptive one. The preposition «من مشهد» is attached to the [notion of] being settled (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached.

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: His words «أسمع بهم»: a past verb in the form of the imperative; the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and the hāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); «أبصر» is like it, and its fāʿil was omitted because what precedes indicates it. The clause «يأتوننا» is muḍāf ilayhi. The clause of rectification (istidrāk) is resumptive; the adverb «اليوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [notion of] being settled (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached.

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: The clause «وأنذرهم» is resumptive. «يوم» is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); it is not an adverb, because the warning does not take place on that day. «إذ» is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (ishtimāl) from يوم. The clause «وهم في غفلة» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object pronoun in «أنذرهم», and the clause «وهم لا يؤمنون» is conjoined to the clause «وهم في غفلة».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: «نحن»: tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun in «إنَّا»; the clause «يرجعون» is conjoined to the resumptive «إنا نحن».

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The clause «إنه كان» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «إبراهيم»; «نبيا» is a second khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: «إذ»: an adverbial noun, a badal (substitute) of {إِبْرَاهِيمَ}. «يا أبتِ»: one addressed in the vocative, in construct, accusative with a fatḥa implied on the letter before the first-person yāʾ, which has been replaced by a tāʾ, and it is muḍāf ilayhi. «لِمَ»: the lām is a preposition; «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of the genitive, whose alif was dropped because the preposition is joined to it, [the phrase being] attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تعبد». «شيئًا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: a little or much availing.

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: «ما»: a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent) of «جاء». The clause «فاتبعني» is conjoined to the clause «جاءني». «أهدك» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the apodosis of an implied condition, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; its two objects are the kāf and «صراطا»; «سويًا»: a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: The clause «إن الشيطان كان» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يمسك» is the object of «أخاف». The preposition «من الرحمن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «عذاب»; the clause «فتكون» is conjoined to the clause «يمسك»; the preposition «للشيطان» is attached to «وليًّا».

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: His words «أراغب أنت»: the hamza is interrogative; «راغب» is the mubtadaʾ (subject); «أنت» is a fāʿil (agent) standing in place of the khabar (predicate); and the preposition «عن آلهتي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «راغب». The clause «يا إبراهيم» is resumptive within the scope of the saying. The lām in «لئن» prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa); the clause «لئن لم تنتهِ» is resumptive within the scope of the saying; the clause «لأرجمَنَّك» is the apodosis of the oath, and the apodosis of the condition (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. The clause «واهجرني» is conjoined to the clause «لئن لم تنته», and «مليًّا» is an adverb of time, i.e.: a long time, attached to «اهجر».

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: «سلام»: the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); beginning with an indefinite is permitted because it indicates a supplication. The clause «سأستغفر» is resumptive within the scope of the saying, and the clause «إنه كان» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ربي».

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: «ما»: a relative noun conjoined to the kāf; the preposition «من دون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ما». «عسى» is a complete past verb, and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is the fāʿil (agent) of «عسى»; the clause «عسى» is resumptive. The preposition «بدعاء» is attached to the khabar (predicate) of كان, «شقيا».

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; «لما» is a particle of [one thing's] occurrence upon [another's] occurrence; the clause «وهبنا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). His words «وكلا»: a fronted first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «نبيا» is the second object.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, the Exalted, {ذكر رَحْمَة رَبك}: al-Farrāʾ said it is nominative by كهيعص, and al-Zajjāj objected to that against him. Al-Akhfash said: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "among what is narrated to you is the mention of the mercy of your Lord" (فِيمَا يقص عَلَيْك ذكر رَحْمَة رَبك).
And it is said that its implied form is "this which is recited is the mention of the mercy of your Lord" (هَذَا الَّذِي يُتْلَى ذكر رَحْمَة رَبك), and the underlying arrangement of the speech is "your Lord's mentioning of His servant Zakariyyā with mercy" (ذكر رَبك عَبده زَكَرِيَّا برحمة).

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying {إِذْ نَادَى ربه}: the governing word (ʿāmil) of إِذْ is ذكر.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying {شيبا}: accusative as an explanation (tafsīr, i.e. tamyīz (specification)); and it is said to be the maṣdar (verbal noun) of شَاب شيبا.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying {يَرِثنِي وَيَرِث}: whoever reads it in the jussive (jazm) makes it the answer to the request, because the request is like the imperative in its ruling. Whoever reads it in the nominative makes it a naʿt (adjective) of الْوَليّ, or [takes it] as a break (qaṭʿ, a new sentence). Its implied form, if you make it an adjective, is "so grant me from Yourself an heir inheriting my knowledge and my prophethood" (فَهَب لي من لَدُنْك وليا وَارِثا علمي ونبوتي).

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying {من الْكبر عتيا}: it is accusative by بلغت, its implied form being "an extreme age" (سنا عتيا). Its origin is عُتُوّ, the maṣdar (verbal noun) of عتا يعتو; they replaced the wāw with a yāʾ and the ḍamma before it with a kasra so that the yāʾ would be sound, because that is lighter, and so that the verse-endings would agree. It has also been read with kasra on the ʿayn (عِتيا), so that the kasra follows the kasra.

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying {سويا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (muḍmar) pronoun in تكلم, or a naʿt (adjective) of ثلاث لَيَال; and likewise بشرا.

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying {وَآتَيْنَاهُ الحكم صَبيا}: صَبيا is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:22-22.t: His saying {مَكَانا قصيا}: an adverb (ẓarf); and it is said to be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) on the implied form "so she made for a distant place with him" (فقصدت بِهِ مَكَانا قصيا).

mekki-muskil:24-24.t:
His saying {فناداها من تحتهَا}: whoever reads the mīm of مِن with kasra (the preposition), the pronoun in فناداها is the pronoun of ʿĪsā (peace be upon him), i.e. "so ʿĪsā called her from beneath her", i.e. from beneath her garments. It is also possible that the pronoun refers to Jibrīl (peace be upon him), and the implied form is "so Jibrīl called her from below her", i.e. from a place lower than her position — as you say "my house is beneath your house", i.e. lower than your house, and "my town is beneath your town", i.e. lower than it; and as He said of Paradise تجْرِي من تحتهَا الْأَنْهَار ("rivers flow beneath it"), i.e. from below it.
So تحت is meant here as the direction facing the thing; thus Jibrīl (peace be upon him) spoke to her from the direction facing her, not from below her. And if the pronoun is for ʿĪsā (peace be upon him), تحت means "below", because the place where ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) was born was below her. What shows that ٤ [Translator's note: a stray numeral, apparently a page marker, stands here in the source] تحت can mean the direction facing a thing is His saying {قد جعل رَبك تَحْتك سريا}, i.e. in the place facing you, not that it was below her. As for reading the mīm of مَن with fatḥa (the relative noun), he makes مَن the fāʿil (agent), and there is then no agent pronoun in فناداها; and مَن in this reading is ʿĪsā (peace be upon him), because he is the one who was below her, so مَن occurs here for a specific referent, though its basic use is for generality. It has also been said that مَن refers to Jibrīl (peace be upon him), as in the first [reading].

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying {تساقط عَلَيْك رطبا}: رطبا is accusative as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz (specification)); and it is said to be the object of هزي. This is only so on the reading of whoever reads it with tāʾ and without doubling, or with doubling, or with fatḥa on the tāʾ and doubling; and in تساقط is the pronoun of the palm tree (النَّخْلَة). It may also be the pronoun of the trunk (الْجذع) — this on the reading of whoever reads it with tāʾ — as they said ذهبت بعض أَصَابِعه ("some of his fingers went", with a feminine verb for a masculine subject annexed to a feminine). As for whoever reads it with yāʾ, there can be in يساقط only the pronoun of the trunk. As for whoever reads it with ḍamma on the tāʾ, without doubling and with kasra on the qāf (تُساقِط), رطبا is the object of تساقط; and it is said to be a ḥāl (circumstantial), with the object implied, its implied form being "its fruit will fall upon you as fresh dates" (تساقط ثَمَرهَا عَلَيْك رطبا). جنيا is a naʿt (adjective). The palm tree indicates the fruit, so its omission is good. And the bāʾ in بجذع is redundant (zāʾida).

mekki-muskil:26-26.t:
His saying {وقري عينا}: accusative as an explanation (tafsīr, i.e. tamyīz (specification)).
His saying {فإمَّا تَرين}: its pattern originally is تفعلين, like تضربين, and the original form of the word is ترأيين. The vowel of the hamza was thrown onto the rāʾ, as is done in ترى; then the vowelled yāʾ, which is the third radical (lām al-fiʿl), was replaced by an alif because it was vowelled and the letter before it had fatḥa; then the alif was dropped because it was quiescent and the yāʾ of the feminine after it was quiescent, so تَرين remained. Then the doubled nūn of emphasis entered, so the nūn of inflection was dropped because of the verb becoming indeclinable (bināʾ), and the yāʾ was given kasra because it was quiescent and the first [element] of the doubled nūn was quiescent. The yāʾ was not dropped, since there is no kasra before it to indicate it, and because the third radical before it had already been dropped. So it became تَرين as it is in the recitation [Translator's note: i.e. تَرَيِنَّ]. So understand that.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t:
His saying {أمك بغيا}: the origin of بغيا is بغوي, so it is on the pattern فعول; but the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ, and the ghayn was given kasra because it adjoins the two yāʾs and so that the quiescent yāʾ would be sound. فعول here has the meaning of فاعلة (active participle), and for that reason it came without a hāʾ [of the feminine] while it is an adjective of a feminine — just as فعول comes without hāʾ for the feminine when it has the meaning of مفعول (passive participle), as in His saying, the Exalted, {فَمِنْهَا ركوبهم}. بغيا is not originally on the pattern فعيل; had it been فعيل, the hāʾ would have been required for the feminine, because فعيل, when it is for the feminine with the meaning of فاعل, requires the hāʾ, as in their saying امْرَأَة رحيمة and عليمة with the meaning of راحمة and عالمة. Since بغي came without hāʾ, it is known that it is فعول and not فعيل.
His saying {يَا أُخْت هَارُون}: the tāʾ in أُخْت is not radical, but it stands in the position of a radical, because it was added for ilḥāq (assimilation to a pattern). For the original of the noun is أخوة on the pattern فعلة; the wāw was dropped and the hamza given ḍamma to indicate the dropped wāw, just as the bāʾ in بنت was given kasra to indicate the dropped yāʾ — the origin of بنت being بنية. So the noun remained on two letters, the hamza and the khāʾ; then the tāʾ was added and it was assimilated to the pattern فُعْل. The diminutive and the plural indicate what we have said, because you restore it to its origin in the diminutive and the plural, saying أخية and أخوات. The dropping of the wāw in it is not according to analogy; and it is said: because of frequent use. Analogy would have been to say in the singular أخاة, changing the wāw into an alif because it is vowelled and the letter before it has fatḥa. Likewise the tāʾ in بنت was added to assimilate the noun to the pattern جِذْع, because its yāʾ was dropped not according to analogy; except that in بنت the yāʾ is not restored in the plural, but it is restored in the diminutive: you say in the diminutive بنية, as you say in أخت أَخِيه [Translator's note: so in the source; the expected diminutive is أُخَيَّة], and you say in the plural بَنَات, and you do not say بنيات as you say أَخَوَات.

mekki-muskil:29-29.t: His saying من كَانَ فِي المهد صَبيا: صَبيا is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and كَانَ is redundant (zāʾida), and the governing word (ʿāmil) of the ḥāl is the [implied] being-settled (al-istiqrār). It is also said that كَانَ here means "occurred / came to be", and in it is its noun as a latent (muḍmar) pronoun, and صَبيا is likewise a ḥāl, its governor being نُكَلِّم; and it is said: كَانَ [Translator's note: the sentence breaks off thus in the source]. Al-Zajjāj said: مَن is for condition (sharṭ), and the meaning is "whoever is in the cradle as a child, how shall we speak to him?"

mekki-muskil:31-31.t: His saying {مَا دمت حَيا}: مَا is in the position of the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "for the time my life lasts"; and it is said to be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). حَيا is the khabar of دمت, and the tāʾ is the noun of دَامَ, because دَامَ is one of the sisters of kāna.

mekki-muskil:32-32.t: His saying {وَبرا بوالدتي}: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to مُبَارَكًا, and مبارك is the second object of جعل. Whoever reads برا in the genitive conjoins it to الصَّلَاة.

mekki-muskil:34-34.t: His saying {قَول الْحق}: whoever reads قول in the nominative implies a mubtadaʾ (subject) and makes قَول الْحق its khabar (predicate), its implied form being "That is ʿĪsā son of Maryam; that is the word of truth" (ذَلِك عِيسَى بن مَرْيَم ذَلِك قَول الْحق), or "this speech is the word of truth". And it is said that the implied pronoun هُوَ is an allusion to ʿĪsā (peace be upon him), because he came into being by the word of Allah (exalted be His mention), and Allah named him a "word" since by the word he came to be; for that reason al-Kisāʾī said, according to this meaning, that قَول الْحق is a naʿt (adjective) of ʿĪsā (peace be upon him). Whoever reads قولا in the accusative takes it as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "I say the word of truth".

mekki-muskil:36-36.t: His saying {وَإِن الله رَبِّي}: whoever reads أَن with fatḥa conjoins it to الصَّلَاة, and whoever reads it with kasra begins a new sentence with it.

mekki-muskil:41-41.t: His saying {إِنَّه كَانَ صديقا نَبيا}: صديق is the khabar of كَانَ, and نبي is a naʿt (adjective) of صديق; and it is said to be a khabar after a khabar.

mekki-muskil:46-46.t: His saying {أراغب أَنْت عَن آلهتي}: رَاغِب is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and أَنْت is nominative by its verbal sense, which is "desiring", and it stands in place of the khabar (predicate). Beginning with an indefinite noun is good because it leans on the interrogative alif before it.

mekki-muskil:47-47.t: His saying {قَالَ سَلام عَلَيْك}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition with its genitive noun is its khabar (predicate). Beginning with an indefinite noun is good here because it carries the meaning of the accusative [i.e. a supplication], and it also carries the meaning of disavowal and parting; so since it conveys benefits, beginning with it is permitted. The rule is that one does not begin with an indefinite noun unless it conveys a benefit to the one addressed.

mekki-muskil:52-52.t: His saying {وقربناه نجيا}: نجيا is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:55-55.t: His saying {مرضيا}: its origin is مرضو on the pattern مفعول, and it is from the roots with wāw, because of their saying الرضْوَان. Then they replaced the wāw with a yāʾ and gave kasra to what precedes it so that the quiescent yāʾ would be sound, and because it is lighter than the wāw.

mekki-muskil:58-58.t: His saying {خروا سجدا وبكيا}: both are accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), and بكيا is then the plural of باك. It is also said that بكيا is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) and is not the plural of باك, its implied form being "they fell down prostrating and wept a weeping" (خروا سجدا وَبكوا بكيا). Its origin in both views is بكويا on the pattern فعول; then the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ and what precedes it given kasra so that the quiescence of the yāʾ would be sound, and because it is lighter. A group of the readers gave kasra to the bāʾ [Translator's note: the source says "the yāʾ"; the reading meant is بِكِيًّا with kasra on the bāʾ] so that kasra follows kasra and so that it is lighter for the work of the tongue.

mekki-muskil:62-62.t: His saying {إِلَّا سَلاما}: accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); and it is said to be a badal (substitute) from لَغْو.

mekki-muskil:63-63.t: His saying {تِلْكَ الْجنَّة الَّتِي نورث من عبادنَا من كَانَ تقيا}: نورث takes two objects because it is a four-letter verb from أورث. The first object is a hāʾ omitted from the ṣila (relative clause) of الَّتِي because of the length of the noun, its implied form being نورثها; and the second object is مَن in His saying من كَانَ تقيا. And مِن is attached to (mutaʿalliq) نورث or to تقي, and the implied form is "That is the Paradise which We give as inheritance to whoever is God-fearing among Our servants" (تِلْكَ الْجنَّة الَّتِي نورثها من كَانَ تقيا من عبادنَا).

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying {قَالَ كَذَلِك}: the kāf is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "he said: the matter is thus" (قَالَ الْأَمر كَذَلِك); so it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject).

mekki-muskil:69-69.t:
His saying {أَيهمْ أَشد على الرَّحْمَن عتيا}: Hārūn the Reader read أَيهمْ in the accusative, making لننزعن govern it. The nominative in أَيهمْ, according to al-Khalīl, is by way of ḥikāya (reported speech): so it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate) is أَشد, the implied form being "Then We shall surely draw out from every sect the one of whom, because of his insolence, it is said: which of these is most insolent?" (ثمَّ لننزعن من كل شيعَة الَّذِي من أجل عتوه يُقَال أَي هَؤُلَاءِ أَشد عتيا). This is like the poet's saying:
... فأبيت لَا حرج وَلَا محروم ...
(And I spent the night neither constrained nor deprived.)
i.e. in the state of one of whom it is said: "neither constrained nor deprived". According to Sībawayh this is nominative by لا, because it is like ليس, and the khabar of ليس is omitted, its implied form being "no one constrained and no one deprived is in my place" (لَا حرج وَلَا محروم فِي مَكَاني); and the yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the reference is to the first-person tāʾ of فأبيت] refers back to the noun of بات, and the clause is the khabar of بات. Whoever makes it ḥikāya makes the reported clause the khabar of بات, and the hāʾ in the implied لَهُ refers back to الَّذِي.
Yūnus held that أي is nominative as a mubtadaʾ by way of ḥikāya, and that the verb, namely لننزعن, is suspended (taʿlīq) so that it does not govern it in its outward form. But according to Sībawayh and al-Khalīl a verb like لننزعن may not be suspended; only verbs such as the verbs of doubt and the like, whose occurrence is not realised, may be suspended.
Sībawayh held that أيا is indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, because for him it is in the position of الَّذِي and مَا; but it differs from them in that annexation (iḍāfa) is permitted in it, so it was made declinable since annexation is permitted in it. Then, when what refers back to it was omitted from its ṣila (relative clause), it was weakened and returned to its origin, which is indeclinability, like الَّذِي and مَا. Had you made the pronoun overt, indeclinability would not be permitted according to him. The implied form of the speech, according to him, is "Then We shall surely draw out from every sect whichever of them is most…" (ثمَّ لننزعن من كل شيعَة أَيهمْ هُوَ أَشد), as you say "We shall surely draw out the one who is most…" (لننزعن الَّذِي هُوَ أَشد). Omitting هُوَ with الَّذِي is ugly; and it has been read تَمامًا على الَّذِي أحسن with أحسن in the nominative on the assumption that هُوَ is omitted — and the omission with الَّذِي is ugly, while with أي it is good. So since أي differs from its sisters, omission with it is good; and when هُوَ was omitted, أيا was made indeclinable on ḍamma.
Sībawayh has been objected to in his view, and it was said: how can an annexed noun (muḍāf) be made indeclinable when it is fully declinable (mutamakkin)? And there is room for consideration in this. Had the omitted pronoun appeared with أي, there would be nothing in أي but the accusative, according to all.
Al-Kisāʾī said: لننزعن falls upon the meaning. Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning of لننزعن is "We shall surely call out", so it does not govern, because it has the meaning of calling. Some of the Kufans said: لننزعن does not govern أَيهمْ only because in it is the meaning of condition and requital, so what precedes it does not govern it; the meaning is "We shall surely draw out from every group, whether they supported one another or did not", as you say ضربت الْقَوْم أَيهمْ غضب ("I struck the people, whichever of them got angry"), the meaning being "whether they got angry or did not". And from al-Mubarrad: أَيهمْ is nominative because it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) شيعة, and the meaning is "from those who sided together [to see] which of them…", i.e. from those who helped one another and looked to see which of them [was most insolent].

mekki-muskil:72-72.t: His saying {فِيهَا جثيا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) if you make it the plural of جاث, and accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) if you do not make it a plural but make it a maṣdar. Its origin in both views is جثوو on the pattern فعول; then the wāw was assimilated into the wāw, and the word became heavy with two ḍammas and two final wāws, so they replaced the wāw with a yāʾ and gave kasra to what precedes it so that the quiescent yāʾ would be sound, and because it is lighter. A group of the readers read it with kasra on the jīm by way of harmony (itbāʿ), for lightness and congruence.

mekki-muskil:75-75.t: His saying {إِمَّا الْعَذَاب وَإِمَّا السَّاعَة}: both are accusative as a badal (substitute) from مَا in His saying {حَتَّى إِذا رَأَوْا مَا يوعدون}.

mekki-muskil:80-80.t:
His saying {ونرثه مَا يَقُول}: the preposition is omitted, its implied form being "and We shall inherit from him what he speaks of" (ونرث مِنْهُ مَا يَقُول), i.e. We shall inherit from him his wealth and his children.
And His saying {ويأتينا فَردا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:87-87.t: His saying {إِلَّا من اتخذ عِنْد الرَّحْمَن}: مَن is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from the latent nominative pronoun in يملكُونَ. It may also be in the position of the accusative as an exception, on the basis that it is not of the same kind as the first [i.e. a disconnected exception].

mekki-muskil:90-90.t: His saying {وتخر الْجبَال هدا}: هدا is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:91-91.t: His saying {أَن دعوا للرحمن ولدا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:92-92.t: His saying {للرحمن أَن يتَّخذ ولدا}: أَن is in the position of the nominative by يَنْبَغِي.

mekki-muskil:93-93.t: His saying {إِن كل من}: إِن has the meaning of مَا (negation). كل is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is إلا آتي الرَّحْمَن. آتي is an active participle, and الرحمن is in the position of the accusative by the [participle of] coming. عبدا is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise فَردا.

muyesser-irab:76-76.t:
﴿ويزيد الله الذين اهتدوا هدى﴾: the wāw is resumptive and the clause after it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; or the wāw is a conjunction, conjoining the clause to the conditional clause reported by "say", i.e.: "And say: Allah increases"; (ويزيد الله الذين اهتدوا) is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (اهتدوا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين), with no grammatical position; and (هدى) is a tamyīz (specification) or a second mafʿūl bihi of (يزيد).
﴿والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير مردا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (الباقيات) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (الصالحات) is a naʿt (adjective); (خير) is the khabar (predicate) of (الباقيات); (عند ربك): the adverb is attached to (خير); (ثوابًا) is a tamyīz; and (وخير مردًّا) is conjoined to (خير ثوابًا).

muyesser-irab:77-77.t: ﴿أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا وقال لأوتين مالا وولدا﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, and the fāʾ is for immediate sequence (taʿqīb); (رأيت) here means "tell me", and (الذي) is its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (كفر بآياتنا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذي), with no grammatical position; (وقال) is conjoined to (كفر); (لأوتين): the lām is the answer to an implied oath, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a hidden pronoun, its implied form being "I" (أنا); (مالًا) is the second mafʿūl bihi of (أوتين), and (ولدًا) is conjoined to ﴿مالًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:78-78.t: ﴿أطلع الغيب أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; (اطلع) is a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is "he", referring back to the disbeliever; (أم) is a conjunction counterbalancing the hamza; (اتخذ) is a past verb, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), referring back to him; (عند الرحمن) is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (اتخذ), and (عهدًا) is the first mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:79-79.t: ﴿كلا سنكتب ما يقول ونمد له من العذاب مدا﴾: (كلا) is a particle of deterrence and rebuke; (سنكتب) is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we" (نحن); (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (يقول) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; (ونمد) is conjoined to (نكتب); ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نمد﴾; (من العذاب) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was an adjective of ﴿مدًّا﴾; and ﴿مدًّا﴾ is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), or a mafʿūl bihi if it has the meaning of "supply" (المدد).

muyesser-irab:80-80.t: ﴿ونرثه ما يقول ويأتينا فردا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (ونرثه) is conjoined to (نمد), and the fāʿil (agent) is "we" (نحن); the hāʾ is accusative by removal of the preposition, and (ما) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the implied sense being: "and We shall inherit from him what he says"; or the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi and (ما) is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from the hāʾ, the meaning being: We shall inherit what he has of wealth, family and children; the clause (يقول) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; (ويأتينا) is conjoined to what precedes, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); (نا) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), fāʿil [Translator's note: so in the source; (نا) in (يأتينا) is in fact an attached pronoun in the position of the mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil having just been given as the latent "he"]; and (فردًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
